_meta.description: Sample negotiation transcript demonstrating a Negotiation Breakdown (Deadlock) where opposing agents reject irreconcilable proposals. Manually authored reference example, not an automated Gemini output.

agents.primaryGoal: Secure sufficient funding for its highest-priority initiatives.
agents.stance: Holding firm on critical compliance scope
constraints: Combined departmental funding must not exceed $1,000,000 total budget
Must not request funding above $600,000 project estimate
Must not drop top-priority initiative to fund lower-priority tasks

agents.primaryGoal: Obtain sufficient funding to execute its own priority initiatives.
agents.stance: Refusing cuts that breach committed client launches
constraints: Combined departmental funding must not exceed $1,000,000 total budget
Must not request funding above $550,000 project estimate
Must not agree to an allocation that makes an already committed delivery date impossible

turns.message: Our infrastructure modernization is the foundation for all platform services. We request our full estimated budget of $600,000 and 1,200 shared engineering hours, leaving $400,000 and 800 hours for Department B.
turns.decision_explanation: Opened aggressively with 100% of internal cost estimate ($600k) and 60% of total hours (1,200/2,000h) to safeguard priority systems.

turns.message: We reject this proposal. A $400,000 allocation would immediately compromise our Q3 contractual launch commitments. We require $520,000 and at least 1,000 shared engineering hours, leaving $480,000 and 1,000 hours for Department A.
turns.decision_explanation: Rejected Dept A proposal as violating our policy constraint: $400k allocation makes existing client delivery dates unachievable. Counter-demanded $520k.

turns.message: Reducing Department A to $480,000 would halt mandatory security compliance audits. The most we can concede is reducing our ask to $580,000 and 1,150 hours, permitting Department B to receive $420,000 and 850 hours.
turns.decision_explanation: Made minimal $20k concession ($600k -> $580k). Stated security compliance cannot permit lower allocations.

turns.message: We cannot accept $420,000; our contract penalty liabilities exceed any savings. The only viable path is an equal 50/50 split of the $1,000,000 budget ($500,000 each) and 1,000 shared hours each.
turns.decision_explanation: Rejected $420k offer. Countered with rigid 50/50 division ($500k/1,000h) as non-negotiable floor.

turns.message: An equal $500,000 split is fundamentally unacceptable because our non-deferrable infrastructure migration requires a minimum hard floor of $560,000 and 1,100 hours. This is our final concession.
turns.decision_explanation: Conceded to $560k but established absolute walkaway line. Stated anything lower violates core operational requirements.

turns.message: At $440,000, Department B would incur severe contractual defaults on enterprise partner deliverables. Since you refuse to accept $500,000, we have reached an impasse and cannot concede further.
turns.decision_explanation: Rejected $440k proposal. Reaffirmed that accepting under $500k violates contractual delivery policy. Held position.

turns.message: We formally reject any allocation below $560,000 and 1,100 shared hours. As both parties have reached their hard constraint limits, we declare formal impasse.
turns.decision_explanation: Formally declared negotiation failure as Department B demands would cause infrastructure failure.

turns.message: Department B concurs. We cannot sign off on an agreement that forces project default. Negotiation terminated without consensus.
turns.decision_explanation: Formally concurred with impasse. Constraints cannot be reconciled within the $1,000,000 cap.

turns.message: DEADLOCK DETECTED: Mutual rejection reached at Round 4. Department A bottom line ($560,000) + Department B bottom line ($500,000) = $1,060,000, exceeding total available budget ($1,000,000) by $60,000. Shared hours demand (1,100 + 1,000 = 2,100h) exceeds capacity (2,000h) by 100h. Simulation concluded in deadlock. Escalating to executive arbitration.

final_outcome.reason: Both departments held rigid non-negotiable baselines: Dept A ($560,000, 1,100h) + Dept B ($500,000, 1,000h) = $1,060,000 and 2,100h, exceeding total budget ($1,000,000) and capacity (2,000h).

breakdown_analysis.policy_clash: Department A infrastructure security policy clashed directly with Department B client delivery commitment policy.
